title: Lux and Foot-Candles: Lighting Design
h1: Lux and foot-candles — the illuminance units that split by border
description: US lighting codes quote foot-candles. Everywhere else quotes lux. Here is the exact factor and how to hit an IES-recommended illuminance in either.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against IES Lighting Handbook 11th ed and CIBSE SLL Code for Lighting

hero: 1 foot-candle = 10.76 lux. The IES recommends 500 lux for office work — that is 46 fc if you are reading a US spec.
body: Illuminance measures how much visible light falls on a surface. The photometric definitions are unambiguous; the units are not. Every US lighting spec is in foot-candles; every European spec is in lux. Design targets translate reasonably but not exactly.

> 1 fc = 10.7639 lx (exact — one lumen per ft² vs one lumen per m²)
> 1 lx = 0.0929 fc
> Sunlight: ~100,000 lx = 9,290 fc
> Overcast day: ~1,000 lx = 93 fc
> Office task: 500 lx = 46 fc
> Living room: 100 lx = 9.3 fc
> Full moon: 0.3 lx = 0.028 fc

Illuminance = luminous flux per unit area. A 1,000-lumen bulb illuminating 1 m² produces 1,000 lx; the same bulb illuminating 10 m² gives 100 lx. It is not the same as brightness (which is luminance in cd/m² — a property of the surface, not the incident light).

IES-RP-1 for offices: 300–500 lx on task, 200 lx ambient. CIBSE LG7: 500 lx on task. EN 12464-1: 500 lx for office reading. Retail: 300–500 lx general, 1,000+ lx accent. Surgery: 20,000–100,000 lx at the operating field. All three organisations align within about 20% on target illuminances — the split is only in the unit shown on the drawing.

A 6 m × 8 m open office, 2.7 m ceiling, target 500 lx on the desk (75 cm floor-to-desk = 1.95 m mounting to task). Room lumens needed = area × illuminance / coefficient of utilisation × light loss factor. 48 m² × 500 lx / (0.65 × 0.85) = 43,400 lm. With 3,000 lm LED downlights: 15 fixtures. Same calculation in US units: 517 ft² × 46 fc / (0.65 × 0.85) = 43,100 lm (arithmetic identical — lumens are the same in both systems).
1 fc = 10.76 lx. Office target: 500 lx = 46 fc. Sunlight: 100,000 lx = 9,290 fc. Same photometry, two labels.

faqs.q: How many lux from a candle at 1 metre?
faqs.a: 1 lux, by definition — the lux is 1 lumen/m², and 1 candela at 1 m produces 1 lumen/m² on a perpendicular surface.
For text, yes. For fine work (electronics, dental, watchmaking), 1,000–5,000 lx is standard. Older adults benefit from higher levels.
Brightness (luminance, cd/m²) depends on surface reflectance. Illuminance is what the source delivers regardless of surface — the right specification for design.
